title: The image of the symmetrization of almost symmetric numerical semigroups
statement: A numerical semigroup S is a set of non-negative integers that contains 0, is closed under addition and has finite complement; its Frobenius number F(S) is its largest gap, its pseudo-Frobenius numbers PF(S) are the gaps x with x + s in S for every positive s in S, t(S) = |PF(S)| is its type, and S is almost symmetric when every gap x has F(S) - x in S, or x and F(S) - x both in PF(S). A numerical set (a set of non-negative integers containing 0, with finite complement) is symmetric with Frobenius number G when exactly one of a and G - a belongs to it for every a in [0, G]. Write the positions 0, 1, ..., F(S) as a word, E at the elements of S and N at its gaps. The symmetrization Phi(S) of Delgado, Suer and Yesil is the numerical set whose word is obtained by deleting the letters at the pseudo-Frobenius numbers other than F(S) (every integer past the shortened word belongs to it); it is symmetric, with Frobenius number G = F(S) - t(S) + 1. For odd G let I(G) be the number of symmetric numerical sets with Frobenius number G that equal Phi(S) for some almost symmetric numerical semigroup S. Determine I(G). The headline cell is G = 43: find more than 1016 such sets (each with a preimage), or prove that there are no others.
submission: Text file: one almost symmetric numerical semigroup per line, given by generators (positive integers with greatest common divisor 1, separated by spaces); lines starting with # are ignored. Every image Phi(S) must have Frobenius number 43, and no two lines may give the same image.
score: the number of different images (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 15 November 2026: 1016 images with Frobenius number 43, one preimage each, from every almost symmetric numerical semigroup with Frobenius number at most 67 (tools/symmetrization_image.py)

context: Almost symmetric numerical semigroups were introduced by Barucci and Froberg as the semigroup case of almost Gorenstein rings; Nari showed that S is almost symmetric exactly when 2 g(S) = F(S) + t(S), g(S) the number of gaps, and that the pseudo-Frobenius numbers below F(S) are symmetric about F(S)/2. Numerical sets correspond to Young diagrams through their words, the setting of Yesil's decompositions (2025). Delgado, Suer and Yesil (2026) delete from the Young diagram of S the rows of its pseudo-Frobenius numbers below F(S) and obtain a symmetric numerical set, and they asked whether every symmetric numerical set arises this way. Every symmetric numerical semigroup with Frobenius number G is its own image (type 1), so I(G) is at least the number of symmetric numerical semigroups with Frobenius number G, and at most the 2^((G-1)/2) symmetric numerical sets. The counts below show that Phi is not onto for G >= 3 (1 of 2 sets at G = 3, 770 of 1,048,576 at G = 41) and that the image is a small, irregular part of the symmetric sets: how fast I(G) grows, and which sets of multiplicity 4 or more are images, is open.
references: M. Delgado, M. Suer, M. Yesil, A symmetrization for almost symmetric numerical semigroups, arXiv:2611.14268 (2026)
V. Barucci, R. Froberg, One-dimensional almost Gorenstein rings, Journal of Algebra 188 (1997) 418-442
H. Nari, Symmetries on almost symmetric numerical semigroups, Semigroup Forum 86 (2013) 140-154
M. Yesil, Young diagram decompositions for almost symmetric numerical semigroups, arXiv:2504.20688 (2025)

novelty.verdict: new. The map Phi was defined in November 2026 (arXiv:2611.14268), whose authors asked only whether it is onto; no count or description of its image was found (arXiv, Crossref, web), and the sequence I(1), I(3), ..., I(41) = 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 9, 12, 18, 25, 32, 50, ... is not in the OEIS.
closest: Delgado, Suer and Yesil (2026): define Phi and ask whether it is onto (the question above refines theirs; the counts answer it in the negative for G >= 3).
Yesil (2025): Young diagram decompositions of almost symmetric numerical semigroups, with a symmetric numerical set attached to a semigroup; no image is counted.
web: web search 15 November 2026: 'symmetrization almost symmetric numerical semigroups symmetric numerical sets image onto' (results: Nari 2013, Yesil 2025, Herzog-Watanabe 2019 on almost symmetric numerical semigroups; nothing on the image of Phi)

first_values.note: Exact for G <= 41: every almost symmetric numerical semigroup with Frobenius number at most 79 was enumerated (tools/src/symmetrization_enum.c, which re-derives the pseudo-Frobenius numbers from the definition at every leaf), and a bound of ours gives every image a preimage with Frobenius number at most max(G, 2G - 5); a separately written Python enumeration agrees for G <= 29, and tools/symmetrization_image.py reproduces every count with preimages of Frobenius number at most 67. For G = 43 to 51 the values are lower bounds from preimages with Frobenius number at most 67 (unchanged from 59 to 67 for G <= 49).

baseline.text: 1016 for G = 43, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 15 November 2026: the preimages in `refs/symmetrization-image.txt`. Upper bound: the 2^21 = 2,097,152 symmetric numerical sets with Frobenius number 43, of which those containing 1 are never images; no better bound is stated here.

cells.title: Images of the symmetrization with Frobenius number {G}
cells.statement: Count the symmetric numerical sets with Frobenius number {G} that are Phi(S) for an almost symmetric numerical semigroup S; I({G}) is their number.
cells.submission: Text file: one almost symmetric numerical semigroup per line (generators), each with an image of Frobenius number {G}, no two with the same image.
cells.exact_how: every almost symmetric numerical semigroup with Frobenius number at most 79 enumerated (tools/src/symmetrization_enum.c); every image has a preimage with Frobenius number at most max(G, 2G - 5)
cells.how: every almost symmetric numerical semigroup with Frobenius number at most 67 (tools/symmetrization_image.py); a lower bound
